blockingProblems: RIGOR, load-bearing technical error about SVMs (line 51). The chapter writes: 'The 62.5% rule escapes that only because thresholding is not part of the object being optimized, so a margin machine has no route to it.' This is false as stated. A soft-margin SVM optimizes over (w, b); the offset b is a primal variable recovered from the KKT conditions. The 62.5% rule the chapter itself constructs, sigma_1 sigma_2 + sigma_3 sigma_4 > 1, is literally a threshold on a linear functional of degree-two monomials, i.e. it sits inside a degree-2 polynomial-kernel SVM's hypothesis class with a nonzero bias. The charitable reading (the SVM minimizes hinge loss plus a norm penalty, not 0-1 accuracy, so it does not select an asymmetric high-accuracy offset) is defensible, but the sentence as written asserts something else and then draws a strong conclusion ('no route') that does not follow. This is the pivot on which the whole paragraph reconciling the 62.5% counterexample with the Ponte-Melko degree-four floor turns.

RIGOR, the same paragraph conflates two distinct estimators' failure modes. Line 51 continues: 'it would pay off only for a machine that happened to pair two opposite bond pairs of one plaquette, two pairs out of the 130,816 that 512 bond spins allow.' A polynomial-kernel SVM does not 'happen to pair' anything; the degree-2 feature map contains every bond pair simultaneously and the dual solution assigns all their coefficients at once. The random-search picture belongs to the gradient-descent argument two paragraphs later and is imported here where it does not apply. The two mechanisms (no margin direction for a kernel machine; no gradient signal for a descent-trained net) are genuinely different and the chapter blurs them.

RIGOR, internal tension in the chapter's own central mechanism (lines 53 and 57). Line 53 concedes 'The gradient is not exactly zero' and locates the surviving signal in the fourth moment, which differs 'only for weight vectors already carrying support on all four bonds of some plaquette.' But a densely initialized 512-input layer generically has support on all 256 plaquettes at step zero, so by the chapter's own analysis the signal is present from the start and the real obstruction is signal-to-noise: the plaquette contribution to E[u^4] is of order 24 * sum_p prod w against a background 3(sum w^2)^2, i.e. suppressed by roughly four orders of magnitude, not absent. The chapter nevertheless states the mechanism as a needle search, 'the network must reach one of the 256 plaquettes among the roughly 2.8 billion ways of choosing four bonds from 512, with nothing en route to tell it that it is getting warmer,' and then builds the convolution explanation on that search picture ('the 256 plaquettes and not the 2.8 billion arbitrary quadruples'). The hedge and the mechanism fight each other at exactly the point where the chapter is making its most original claim.

STRUCTURE, unreconciled claim about what the founding paper measured. Line 9 states flatly that on the square lattice 'Carrasquilla and Melko do not claim to have discovered T_c there.' Line 15 then reports, from the same paper's published version, a square-lattice finite-size-scaling collapse yielding T_c = 2.266 +/- 0.002, and line 87 treats that number as a legitimate determination ('The 2.266(2) comes from collapsing the whole averaged-output curve for L up to 60'). Extracting a value by finite-size scaling and claiming to have discovered T_c are of course different things, but the chapter never says so, and a reader who took line 9 seriously will read line 15 as a contradiction. The distinction is the chapter's own best material and it is left on the floor.

STRUCTURE, the stated thesis does not cover the chapter's center of mass. The promise is made at line 5: 'Why an output with no temperature in it should sharpen at the rate finite-size scaling requires is a question the founding paper does not ask, and the answer also explains its most striking effect.' That debt is paid, well, in the Kim-Kim section. But the square-ice and gauge-theory sections (lines 23 to 59) are roughly forty per cent of the chapter and advance an entirely separate argument about moment degeneracy, gradient starvation and architectural priors, which the opening never signals and which the closing never gathers. Two good chapters are sharing a set of covers.
styleViolations: No em dashes, no '--', no bullet or numbered lists, no end-of-chapter summary or recap. Hard rules are clean.

TERMINOLOGY: 'degeneracy' carries three distinct technical meanings and the third is then used bare. Line 25, extensive ground-state degeneracy of the Coulomb phase; line 39, topological degeneracy destroyed by restitching; line 43, 'a degeneracy of moments,' coined once. Thereafter line 55 says 'Degeneracy does not forbid the fully connected network anything' and line 57 says 'degeneracy takes the gradient away' with no qualifier, in paragraphs sitting between the other two senses. The author plainly knows the difference; the page does not make it.

NOTATION: the symbol q is overloaded. Line 3 uses q for the antiferromagnetic ordering wavevector, q = (pi/a, pi/a). Line 5 uses <q>_T for the ensemble-averaged network output, before that object has been defined. Line 72 then formally defines q as the Kim-Kim network output. Meanwhile Q_v is the square-ice vertex charge. Two of these collide inside two paragraphs of each other.

The opening sentence is a 60-word architecture spec sheet (hidden layer, sigmoid count, softmax width, cost function, regularizer, optimizer) before any reason to care has been supplied. The chapter's real opening is paragraph two, 'A structural oddity sits underneath that success,' which is excellent.

Line 51 is a single 90-word sentence carrying three semicolon-joined clauses, an aside about lattice size, and a parenthetical caveat about what the paper does not state. It is the least readable passage in the chapter and it is also the one containing the SVM error.
factProblems: CHRONOLOGY, reversed order implied for Broecker and Ch'ng. Line 65 introduces Broecker, Carrasquilla, Melko and Trebst with 'made the opposite choice,' immediately after the Ch'ng, Carrasquilla, Melko and Khatami Hubbard work, which reads as a response. The packet gives Broecker as arXiv:1608.07848 posted 28 August 2016 and Ch'ng as arXiv:1609.02552 posted 8 September 2016; Broecker came first by eleven days. The chapter supplies no dates for either, so the reader cannot correct the impression.

CHRONOLOGY, Ohtsuki and Ohtsuki framed as successors rather than independent contemporaries. Line 67, 'In October 2016 Tomoki Ohtsuki and Tomi Ohtsuki went further.' The packet outline is explicit that they 'had independently applied deep learning to random two-dimensional electron systems in 2016.' 'Went further' asserts a line of descent the packet does not support.

CHRONOLOGY, the chapter is almost dateless. October 2016 for Ohtsuki is the only anchor in the body. Carrasquilla and Melko are never dated (packet: arXiv v1 5 May 2016, Nature Physics 2017), so the reader cannot place Ohtsuki relative to the founding paper, cannot tell how much later 'Ponte and Melko later' or 'Suchsland and Wessel later' means, and cannot situate the seven-year gap to Chertenkov, Burovski and Shchur (2023). The citation block carries the years; the argument does not.

Everything else checks out against the packet. Attributions, architectures, accuracies (94%/99% at L = 10/40; 99% square ice; 100% gauge CNN; 50%/55% after plaquette flips), Onsager 2/ln(1+sqrt2), triangular 3.63581 vs 4/ln3 = 3.640957, toy network 3.63403, published-version collapse 2.266(2) and nu = 1.0(2) and 3.65(1) with the two-source provenance correctly disclosed, Kim-Kim 2.267(1)/nu = 0.94(2)/3.637/4.4695/0.51815/0.63/4.51152(1), Chertenkov ResNet-50 shift pattern at L = 96,144,216 versus 48,72, Ferdinand-Fisher fits 2.2691(4) and 2.2687(4). Both packet CORRECTIONS that bear on this chapter are honoured: Broecker is described as classifying the sampled Green's function with the auxiliary field explicitly ruled insufficient, and Ohtsuki is described with no critical exponents and with the symplectic SU(2) and disordered-Chern-to-Anderson transitions, including the authors' own deferral of nu. No unpacketed person, paper, venue or attributed number appears. Eponyms are named where used (Onsager, Elitzur, Wolff, Adam, Ferdinand-Fisher). Every criticism of published work names its target, including the sharp and correct catch at line 85 that Chertenkov et al. identify their CNN-on-Ising case with Carrasquilla-Melko when the square and triangular results came from the fully connected network. The chapter's own arithmetic is right: C(512,2) = 130,816; 256 vertices x 6 pairs = 1,536; C(512,4) = 2,829,877,120; balanced accuracy (1/2 + 3/4)/2 = 0.625; sigma(-mu) = 1/4 gives mu = ln 3; sigma'(-ln3) = 3/16 and sigma''(-ln3) = 3/32 give Lambda*z = (3/32)Lambda(y^2 - 4delta); Q_v = 0 gives a same-vertex pair correlation of -1/3.
whatWouldMakeItAAA: Three surgical fixes and one structural one. First, repair line 51. The chapter has already earned the hard part by constructing the 62.5% counterexample and then showing, via chi[d>1] = (1/4)(1 + s1s2 + s3s4 + s1s2s3s4) and d^2 = 2 + 2 s1s2s3s4, that the separating content was degree four all along. That is a beautiful piece of reasoning and it does not need the false claim that an SVM does not optimize its threshold. Say instead that the machine minimizes hinge loss under a norm penalty rather than 0-1 error, that the symmetric structure of the two ensembles leaves the loss with no preferred asymmetric offset, and that the coefficients on all 130,816 pair monomials are set at once by the dual rather than searched. Then keep the random-search picture strictly for the gradient argument, where it belongs. Second, make the fully connected failure a signal-to-noise argument rather than a needle-search one, since the chapter's own fourth-moment analysis already delivers the numbers: a dense weight vector has plaquette support from initialization, but the plaquette term enters E[u^4] at order 24 sum_p prod w against a background 3(sum w^2)^2, and that ratio, not the count of quadruples, is what convolution repairs by making every four-body product a plaquette product. The convolution paragraph survives intact and becomes true rather than merely vivid. Third, spend two sentences reconciling line 9 with line 15: the paper declines to claim discovery of T_c on the training lattice, and separately extracts 2.266(2) from a collapse of the whole curve across sizes, and the difference between a value read off a labelled boundary and a value read off the rate at which a curve steepens is the chapter's own thesis, so it should be stated where the tension first appears rather than left for the reader to assemble at line 87. Structurally, either widen the promise in paragraph two to cover both arguments, saying openly that the chapter will ask two questions of one paper, what its output measures and why one architecture can find a four-body constraint while another cannot, or move the gauge-theory material to its own chapter and let this one be the finite-size-scaling argument at full strength. Finally, put four dates in the body: May 2016 for the preprint, the ordering of the Broecker and Ch'ng preprints as they actually fell, and 2023 for Chertenkov, so the reader can feel the seven years between the founding claim and the verdict on its estimator. Do those and this is better than most of what university presses publish on the subject; the mechanism work in the square-ice and Kim-Kim sections is already well past that bar.
